source.title: Estimating Implicit Regularization in Deep Learning
source.authors: Joseph H. Rudoler; Kevin Tan; Giles Hooker; Konrad P. Kording

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests a scalar ridge penalty as a replacement for dropout and reports that it does not recover dropout's test performance in the tested configuration, refining the scope of dropout's regularization effects.
record.gate_note: The dropout experiment compares held-out accuracy for dropout-trained models, no-dropout controls, and explicit fitted-ridge replacements. Other gradient-matching estimates and cited results do not measure the claim versions' named outcomes.
record.test_reason: The dropout-versus-no-dropout comparison directly tests V6 using the same intervention and held-out classification measure as the original dropout work. Failure of a fitted ridge replacement does not qualify V6, which claims no equivalence between dropout and ridge.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the dropout-specific conclusion: ridge projections reveal variation across configurations, but their low gradient fit and unsuccessful replacement show that scalar ridge incompletely describes dropout. The paper's broader conclusion is that gradient matching can recover known explicit and theoretically predicted implicit regularization, subject to identification and modeling assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The study estimates gradient-matching regularizers and tests an explicit ridge replacement for dropout; it does not reproduce the original sources' dropout experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the fitted dropout ridge coefficient varies with dropout rate, network width, and depth; the tested replacement comparison is limited to depth 3, width 256, dropout rate 0.3.

fits_no_version.finding: Fitted ridge replacements achieve median test accuracy of 97.85%, versus 98.345% for dropout, and perform worse in all ten paired seeds.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Endpoint-fitted scalar ridge penalties do not reproduce dropout's held-out performance in this MNIST configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 6 reports qualitative associations between estimated implicit gradient regularization, smaller squared gradients, and higher test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Estimated implicit gradient regularization is associated with held-out accuracy in the selected MNIST runs; this does not test magnitude-aware sharpness or post-interpolation width generalization.

record.problems: The held-out performance replacement comparison covers one architecture and dropout setting with ten seeds. The paper reports medians and a paired mean shortfall but no uncertainty interval for these accuracies. The paper also notes that endpoint estimates can reflect residual optimization gradients and that the fitted scalar ridge has low gradient fit.
record.rows_left_out: No other results meeting the row criteria for the tested claim version were reported. Gradient-fit diagnostics and estimated ridge coefficients do not measure the held-out error named by V6.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the corresponding natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy comparison.
Whether widening beyond the zero-training-error threshold keeps lowering test error under training to convergence.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity or transferred initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.

Convolutional classifiers, very small training sets, underfitting from excessive dropout, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay with data augmentation. Held-out dropout benefits are reported for only one architecture and dropout rate.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's V6 limits_scope verdict for ridge replacement. V6 does not predict that ridge reproduces dropout. The shared stopping rule allowed different training durations, so the accuracy comparison is conditional on that training procedure.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not evaluated.
No width sweep tests test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
No adaptive-versus-SGD generalization comparison is reported.
No large-batch generalization-gap comparison is reported.

The study tests one dropout configuration for held-out accuracy and its fitted-ridge replacement; it does not test very small training sets, excessive dropout, or removing dropout and weight decay together with data augmentation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures is reported.
No memorized-example removal experiment is reported.

rows.subject: depth-3, width-256 MNIST classifiers trained with dropout rate 0.3 (10 seeds; median)
rows.operation_detail: Train with dropout rate 0.3; evaluate test accuracy at the stopping endpoint.
rows.locator: Appendix H.4.1, Validation by explicit replacement
rows.note: The paper reports the median across the ten dropout targets.
rows.check: Values are correct. Specify three hidden ReLU layers, 54,000 training examples, and no batch normalization or explicit weight decay.

rows.subject: depth-3, width-256 MNIST classifiers trained without dropout (10 seeds; median)
rows.operation_detail: Train without dropout as the no-penalty control; evaluate test accuracy.
rows.locator: Appendix H.4.1, Validation by explicit replacement
rows.note: The median no-dropout accuracy is lower than the dropout target accuracy.
rows.check: This control supplies the comparison establishing the dropout benefit: median accuracy rises from 97.86% to 98.345%. Its lower accuracy without dropout is not a partial dropout effect.

rows.subject: depth-3, width-256 MNIST classifiers trained with fitted ridge penalty (10 seeds; median)
rows.operation_detail: Replace dropout with the endpoint's fitted explicit ridge penalty; evaluate test accuracy.
rows.uncertainty: Mean shortfall of 0.508 percentage points; not stated for the median.
rows.locator: Appendix H.4.1, Validation by explicit replacement
rows.note: The fitted ridge replacements had lower accuracy than their paired dropout targets for all ten seeds.
rows.check: The numbers are correct, but this is performance of the study's fitted replacement method. Failure to reproduce dropout with scalar ridge does not measure a limitation named by V6.

relationships.condition: MNIST fully connected ReLU classifiers with three hidden layers of width 256, dropout rate 0.3, ten seeds, and training-loss-based stopping.
relationships.reason: R1–R2 report median test accuracy of 98.345% with dropout versus 97.86% without it, a 0.485 percentage-point improvement; no accuracy uncertainty interval is reported.
relationships.display_finding: Median test accuracy rose from 97.86% to 98.345%, without an uncertainty interval and with potentially different stopping epochs.
